chief_complaint: Increasing shortness of breath and fatigue for the past week, worse with exertion.
doctor_notes: Patient presents with worsening dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea. Physical exam reveals bilateral crackles in lung bases and peripheral edema. ECG shows sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy. Chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular congestion. Current medications reviewed. Will adjust diuretic dose and continue antihypertensives. Education provided on dietary sodium restriction and daily weights.

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Doctor, I've been feeling so tired lately, and I can't catch my breath even when I'm just walking to the kitchen.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: I understand, Eleanor. You mentioned this has been going on for about a week. Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or feet?

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Yes, my ankles have been quite puffy, and my rings are feeling tight.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: Okay, based on your symptoms and what I'm seeing, it looks like your heart failure might be a bit more active right now. We'll need to adjust your medication to help manage that.

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Will I be okay? I'm worried.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: We will work to get you feeling better. We'll increase your water pill and check on your blood pressure medications. It's important to keep an eye on your diet, especially salt intake, and weigh yourself every morning. I'll also schedule you for a follow-up appointment in two weeks.

follow_up_actions: Monitor blood pressure and weight daily
